Keyvany’s New G850 Is a Mercedes-AMG G 63 That Looks Like a Confused Mansory
10 photos
Photo: Instagram | keyvany
Is it a bird? Is it a plane? Nope, it’s just another tuned G-Wagen that looks like it tries too much to be a Mansory. However, it has nothing to do with the latter company, because, as mentioned above, this project came directly from Keyvany’s portfolio.
Following in the footsteps of other brash builds that this tuner has recently signed, it does not look kitschy on the outside, but then again, you can blame it on the glossy black overall look. That’s because this color tends to hide bold makeovers like a champ, and we reckon that if this thing were presented in a more vibrant color, joined by some forged carbon accents, then the word “kitschy” would have been found in the title.
Keyvany surely knows how to attract attention, and its latest take on the Mercedes- AMG G 63 is definitely a head-turner, albeit not for the right reasons. That’s because it tries too much to look beastly. But then again, we have seen far worse takes on the modern-day G-Wagen over the years, including some from this company, like the so-called G950 that we covered here a little over a month ago, which had a similar makeover, albeit with a different exterior color.
This ride is called the Keyvany G850, and is said to be an entirely new project. It features redesigned fender flares that are not necessarily better looking than the stock ones, as well as new side skirts with cutouts in front of the rear wheels for the side-exit exhaust tips, which are now three instead of two on each side. The front fender trim is new, there is a splitter attached to the front bumper, and chances are that the latter component has also come from the tuner’s shelves.
Photo: Instagram | keyvany We can also see that the grille of this tuned Mercedes-AMG G 63 has also come from Keyvany’s portfolio. It has different slats, and the tuner’s logo sits right in the middle. The hood is on the more muscular side of things, as it has a big scoop right in the middle. The central part of the front bumper is home to an aftermarket light strip, and we can see another one mounted above the front windscreen.
It looks like there are some aftermarket panels on the sides, thus contributing to this vehicle’s wider overall nature, and there are also some fake vents behind the rear fender flares. The rear bumper seems to be entirely new as well, and it features a new diffuser attached to it that extends on the lower part toward the car’s sides. The double-bubble-like roof spoiler is another novelty, just like the trim on the rear pillars, and the custom spare wheel holder attached t othe rear door.
Keyvany’s logos decorate various parts of the exterior, and this modified Mercedes-AMG G 63 also sits a bit closer to the asphalt, suggesting that a lowering kit is part of the makeover. The concave wheels are also new, and while they are not exactly the most inspiring, we’ve seen worse choices. Like far worse.
Our better halves know what the interior color is called, but to us, it’s an orange-y theme, joined by new trim, the Keyvany logo on various components, new seatbelts, redesigned seats, and a few other bits and bobs that make this modern-day G-Wagen stand out more. And this is definitely one vibrant-looking cockpit, though it does not necessarily fit the design of this model, does it?
Photo: Instagram | keyvany Either way, the tuner’s work hasn’t ended here, because this Mercedes-AMG G 63 also has more power. The G850 in its name reveals that the revised output is now rated at 850 metric horsepower, which equals 838 brake horsepower and 625 kilowatts. The acceleration and top speed haven’t been mentioned at the time of writing, but then again, Keyvany did not have much to say about this build, as you can see from the social media post embedded at the bottom of the page.
As for the standard Mercedes-AMG G 63, it comes with 577 hp (585 ps/430 kW) and 627 lb-ft (850 Nm) of torque from its 4.0-liter bi-turbocharged V8 engine. The lump drives all four wheels through a nine-speed automatic transmission, and the automaker reveals that 0-60 mph (0-97 kph) takes as little as 4.2 seconds, which is impressive, given that this model is anything but a blue-blooded crossover. In fact, it’s a body-on-frame truck that will hit 137 mph 9220 kph) flat-out, or 149 mph (240 kph) with the optional AMG Performance Pack.
One must fork out a minimum of $198,750 for a brand-new Mercedes-AMG G 63 from the 2027 model year, before destination, options, and dealer fees, and a lot more if they somehow dream about owning a Keyvany, because these things may not be the prettiest G-Wagens out there, but they do cost a pretty penny.
